title: Parseval identity for the sign lift of a Boolean function
statement:
Let $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be a Boolean-valued function, and let $g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be its $\pm 1$ lift, given by $g(x) = (-1)^{f(x)}$. Then the Fourier coefficients $\hat g(S) = \langle g, \chi_S\rangle$, taken over all subsets $S \subseteq [n]$, satisfy
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \hat g(S)^2 \;=\; 1.
\]
hypotheses_covered: f is a function from the Boolean hypercube to {0,1} (Bool)
g is the ±1 lift of f, i.e. g(x) = (-1)^{f(x)}
the sum ranges over all subsets S of [n]
replaced:
For every $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$, the $\pm 1$ lift
$g = \texttt{BoolBLR.lift\_pm1}\,f$ has unit Fourier mass:
\[
  \sum_{S \subseteq [n]} \hat{g}(S)^2 \;=\; 1.
\]
